note: Item ids and names are OWASP's. Summaries are SoCHarness's own one-line paraphrases; read the official pages for the full text (CC BY-SA 4.0). ATLAS links are a curated SoCHarness crosswalk, not an official mapping.

items.name: Prompt Injection
items.summary: Input, typed by a user or hidden in content the model reads, changes the model's behaviour against the application's intent.

items.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
items.summary: The application reveals personal data, credentials, business secrets or model details in its output.

items.name: Supply Chain
items.summary: Third-party models, datasets, adapters and packages bring in tampered, vulnerable or badly licensed components.

items.name: Data and Model Poisoning
items.summary: Training, fine-tuning or embedding data is manipulated to plant bias, backdoors or degraded behaviour.

items.name: Improper Output Handling
items.summary: Model output is passed to browsers, shells, databases or other systems without validation or encoding.

items.name: Excessive Agency
items.summary: The application gives the model more functionality, permissions or autonomy than its task needs.

items.name: System Prompt Leakage
items.summary: System prompts expose secrets, rules or internal logic that an attacker can read and use.

items.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
items.summary: Retrieval stores and embeddings leak across tenants, accept poisoned entries or reveal source data.

items.name: Misinformation
items.summary: Confident but false or unsupported output is trusted and acted on.

items.name: Unbounded Consumption
items.summary: Uncontrolled requests exhaust compute or budget, or are used to copy the model's behaviour.

items.name: Agent Goal Hijack
items.summary: Injected instructions or poisoned content redirect what the agent is trying to achieve.

items.name: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
items.summary: The agent uses tools it is allowed to use in unsafe ways, chains or amounts.

items.name: Identity and Privilege Abuse
items.summary: Delegated identities, cached credentials or inherited roles let the agent act beyond what its user may do.

items.name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Third-party tools, plugins, MCP servers or agents are compromised or change behaviour after they are trusted.

items.name: Unexpected Code Execution
items.summary: Generated or injected code runs in the agent's environment or connected systems without the intended checks.

items.name: Memory and Context Poisoning
items.summary: Malicious entries in memory, history or retrieved context keep steering the agent across sessions.

items.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
items.summary: Messages between agents can be spoofed, altered or replayed because channels are not authenticated or protected.

items.name: Cascading Failures
items.summary: One faulty or compromised step spreads through connected agents and automations faster than people can stop it.

items.name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
items.summary: Convincing agent output leads people to approve harmful actions they would otherwise question.

items.name: Rogue Agents
items.summary: An agent drifts from or works against its intended purpose while still appearing to operate normally.
